title: T-shirts — Athlete program level branding – No sponsorship
slide_intent: Teach a designer to reserve space on an athlete’s uniform for its competitive job, including the team number or event identification.
strategic_value: Special Olympics can remain identifiable across team colors and uniform configurations while keeping competition clothing free of sponsor branding.
demonstration: Three diagrams reduce the program mark from a large centered treatment to a horizontal lockup and a crest beside a number. A row of colored shirts demonstrates light and dark mark treatments.
practical_value: Choose roughly 100 mm, 70 mm or 30 mm symbol height for the large, medium or crest application shown. Check the print color against the actual fabric.

content_islands.name: Uniform guidance
content_islands.spec: Set the no-sponsorship heading above notes on the three placements and their approximate dimensions. Keep the approved logo-color note distinct.

content_islands.name: Placement diagrams
content_islands.spec: Align three white shirts at the top. Dimension the large and medium marks and show a number with the crest treatment.

content_islands.name: Fabric comparison
content_islands.spec: Arrange the colored shirts underneath. Group darker and lighter bases so the change in mark contrast can be compared.
